business_rules.statement: A tenant may make the platform stricter than default and may never make it looser than the platform floor, and the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value rather than logging it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Tenant administration area save, validated against the Super Admin tenant-configuration registry

business_rules.statement: A tenant cannot reach an operational state while no Tenant Admin account is active.
Every tenant-administration-area setting change writes an audit event in the same transaction as the change.
A tenant-administration-area value looser than the platform floor is rejected at entry with a message naming the floor, not accepted and logged.
The workspace is created only from the Super Admin platform console, never from any tenant surface.
The tier record carries entitlements, limits and thresholds and never price metadata, because pricing and invoicing sit entirely outside the platform.
The platform enforces that at least one Tenant Admin always exists.
The Frontline Worker Application is unreachable for this tenant until at least one worker identity and one enrolled device exist.
The invitation email is generated from the English or Spanish locale file matching the invited contact's recorded language preference, and is never machine-translated at runtime.
Two live invitations to one tenant is a security defect; issuing a second invitation moves the original explicitly to expired.
The qualification gate is the only configurable gate on the platform, and its own floor is notify-only: no silent posture exists.
Every setting screen displays each setting's platform default and its floor or ceiling alongside the current value.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry with a message naming the bound, and no configuration record and no accepted-setting audit event are written; a rejection event is written.
The Severity 1 minimum action bundle renders as locked for every tenant role including the Tenant Admin.
A Site cannot be omitted while shifts exist, and the timezone is inherited by every Shift bound beneath it.
No qualification may be entered by the worker who holds it.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen — the one-transaction audit guarantee makes a partial setting/audit state impossible by construction.
A recertification expiry that does not postdate the previous expiry is refused with the rule stated; no partial record is created and the worker's existing qualification state stands unchanged.

The Job state machine is draft to pending_approval to active to archived; both Tenant Admins and Supervisors can create Jobs; the approver is the tenant's Quality Manager or a designated equivalent approver.
Segregation of duties is absolute — the creator of a Job cannot approve that same Job, and if the creator also holds the approver role the platform routes approval to a second qualified approver.
A Job cannot transition from draft to active without an approval by a user who is not its creator.
Submission is refused where no eligible second approver exists, with the reason stated.
No run may be created against a Job that is not active.
The Approve control renders disabled with the segregation-of-duties reason for the creator, and is never merely hidden.
Rejection requires a categorised reason and returns the Job to draft with the reason attached.
Job Owner defaults to the creator and is reassignable, and confers no permissions.

The approval chain is Author, then Reviewer, then Release Authority; the Reviewer must be a different person from the Author, no role performs two stages on one submission, and the Release Authority cannot be bypassed.

Versioning is semantic vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; a patch carries no operating-behaviour change and auto-adopts, while minor and major are the notified classes decided by the Job Owner; a republish description is mandatory at every republish and doubles as the worker-facing change notice on the first screen of the next execution.
At least one severity mapping is required per measurement screen.
An incomplete locale blocks publication in that locale, and no runtime machine translation occurs anywhere.
A work package is generated per run and pinned immutably for the life of that run.
Machine-drafted instruction levels are visibly marked as drafted and unreviewed and cannot reach a published version without passing the full review chain.
No draft content is reachable from the Frontline Worker Application, the Client Command Center, or any packaged run.
A change altering operating behaviour cannot be published as a patch.
Publication changes no in-flight run's pinned version.
A run cannot be started on a device that has not staged and validated that run's pinned package.
A run whose package has not arrived displays as not-yet-ready and never as missing or silently absent.
The Frontline application's sync indicator shows online state, last-synced time and pending-captures count at all times.

The login is the credential, not the device: a worker's identity, qualifications, language preference and attribution travel with them onto whatever conformant device they pick up, and a shared tablet confers nothing by itself.
Navigation is forward-driven with read-only review of prior screens and append-only correction after commit.
No pace figure, timer against expectation, or comparison to other workers is rendered anywhere in the Frontline Worker Application.
business_rules.applies_to: every module, state and release of this scope

business_rules.statement: A committed capture is immutable; corrections are appended with who, when and what changed.
A login on an unexpected device succeeds and is flagged in the audit trail, with no hard block at V1.
Every deterministic gate, specification check and severity classification evaluates identically online and offline.
Captured media is written to the application's encrypted store and never to the device gallery.
The Client Command Center shows an offline cell's last-synced picture with its age and never blanks the tile.
No coaching card is presented offline, and the authored work instruction is presented in its place.
The deterministic layer — hard gates, deviation detection, and severity-band classification — runs on-device and offline, mandatorily.
Sync is continuous when connected, resumes automatically on reconnection, and is never a worker action; a manual control exists only as a convenience.
Media is evicted from the device only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, never on the strength of an attempted upload.

Severity 1's minimum bundle is automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation, platform-fixed; the freeze lands on the Lot where a lot exists, the Unit where work is serialized, otherwise the Run.
Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly, with supervisors requesting release with a note and no exceptions by work type, risk class, or tag.
A hold's lifecycle is displayed honestly as issued, propagating, in force per device, because commands apply at each device's next sync and never as instant remote control.
No agent participates in detection or classification at any point.
A hold is never displayed as in force on a device that has not confirmed it.
A Severity 2 classification places no hold on the lot, the unit, or the run.
A failure to persist the hold fails the capture transaction rather than accepting the capture without the hold.
Every accepted capture carries both device time and server-receipt time, and ordering follows server receipt.
A write whose device clock deviates beyond the tenant threshold is flagged skew-affected and cannot win a conflict unreviewed.
A Severity 1 runtime event automatically creates a Critical anomaly with its containment record attached.
The Release hold control is enabled only for the Quality Manager role and is rendered disabled with the rule for every other role.
No surface offers any path to edit or delete evidence.
An anomaly cannot be resolved without a closure note.
A hold reaches in force only when every relevant device has confirmed.
No surface offers any control that forces a command onto a device.
A command a device cannot validate is rejected explicitly and never silently discarded.
A skew-flagged write is excluded from automatic resolution and from Resolve All, and requires an individual resolution with a reason.
No version is ever deleted, and no value is ever edited from this panel.
A conflict whose values straddle a specification limit triggers a deterministic deviation evaluation.
No gate item executes without a human decision, and none expires silently.
Every gate item card leads with a counted scope of impact.
No Lane-B proposal changes any configured value without a Quality Manager's approval.
In-flight runs remain pinned and finish on the version they started on.
An undecided proposal never expires and is flagged stale at 30 days.
The Shift Handoff Agent creates and modifies no operational record and carries no approval gate.
Opening the brief and acknowledging it are two distinct, separately timestamped events.
Acknowledgement never blocks a shift from starting.
Emerging-pattern watch items are visible to Supervisors and above and never to Workers.
The 14, 7, 1 and 0 day warnings all fire and cannot be removed or delayed by any tenant setting.
At expiry under the strict posture, the current run may complete and the next assignment is blocked.
A never-held qualification requires Quality Manager authorisation.
A clearance lapses automatically at the end of its tenant-set duration and the block re-applies at the next gate evaluation.
A second clearance in the same Area in the same shift routes to the Quality Manager regardless of worker.
No on-device control permits any role to override a qualification gate.
A blocked run parks and the worker's other assigned runs remain available.
A parked run resumes at its exact blocked position with prior captures intact.
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing a hold, a qualification, an authorization, an approval, a suspension, or a device command.
Worker-finished stands the run as submitted; complete arrives only when every assigned device has uploaded everything.
A forced sync is required before a designated high-risk sign-off; the supervisor sign-off screen type is one, an ordinary worker signature is not.

A conflict whose two values disagree beyond the screen's specification limits is passed to the rule-based deviation mechanism, because two materially different readings of the same capture is a quality event.
The gate exists for proposed interventions beyond pre-authorised policy, and only for those; every gate item leads with the scope of impact in counted objects.

Lane A refinements tune themselves, are logged and reversible, and change nothing a person configured; Lane B changes are always surfaced as evidence-backed proposals for human approval and are never auto-approved.

On approval the package test decides where the change lands: package-borne values auto-publish a patch version and distribute per the tenant's adoption timing, and server-only values apply immediately.

Escalations resolve to people on shift; where nobody holding the target role is on shift, delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, explicitly marked as a fallback delivery.
Qualification requirements on the Job are authoritative, and validation runs at assignment, at run start, and at override-carrying screens.
Unit mode is declared per Job: serialized, lot, or none.

Packages for the shift's known runs are pre-synced at shift start while the device has connectivity, and a run assigned mid-shift is pulled lazily when the device is next connected; until a run's package has arrived, the run is shown as not-yet-ready rather than silently missing.

There is no on-device worker override of a hard gate and none is offered; if a gate cannot be evaluated for any reason, the terminal safe state is refusal to advance — the platform fails closed on a gate.

Delivery/staging at shift start

decisions.status: Client Decision Required — owed by the client

decisions.question: What does the device do when its storage fills?
options: Warn worker and supervisor before the limit, refuse new media capture, never evict unconfirmed evidence (Recommendation — R&D)

decisions.impact: Long offline shift with photograph-heavy screens

decisions.question: On reconnection, does a device upload pending captures before or after pulling pending commands?
options: Commands first (safety argument)
Captures first (data-integrity argument)
Option C: three phases split by urgency
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option C, adopted 2026-08-14: phase 1 pulls and applies stop-class commands (suspension in all three states, device de-authorisation, remote wipe, any tenant compliance stop); phase 2 uploads every pending capture with nothing discarded; phase 3 applies the enabling classes of lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, and version change. Beyond phase 1 the upload queue is never blocked on command processing, and a fencing token is attached so a stale command arriving after a newer one is rejected.
decisions.status: adopted working position — open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Reconnection ordering; command versus capture interleaving

decisions.question: Does every action-agent step route through a human gate, or only proposals beyond pre-authorised policy?
options: §3.7 and §6.6.1: the runtime gate exists only for proposals beyond pre-authorised policy
§8.3.2/§8.3.3: action agents change state and every one routes through a human gate before any effect; Prevention Agent labelled 'action, gated'
decisions.adopted_working_position: The first reading declared per agent: the Deviation and Containment Agent's governance binding is runtime human gate for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment; the second reading is recorded explicitly rather than dismissed
decisions.impact: Whether an offline mid-run checklist launch requires a gate

decisions.question: What is the nobody-on-shift escalation default?
options: Escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.adopted_working_position: Escalating to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift and marked as a fallback delivery, carried as an open drafting value
decisions.impact: Gate item and escalation routing when no role holder is on shift

decisions.question: Do Plant Manager and Quality Director exist as roles, given §3.5 fixes five roles?

§3.5 fixes five roles, states there is no Quality Director, and makes Plant Manager a persona

options: Plant Manager view (source)
Tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery (recommendation)

decisions.adopted_working_position: This walk states authorities by named role — Quality Manager for release, Supervisor for request and acknowledgement

The agent launches it server-side

contradictions.description: Surface naming: Statement of Work names it Delivery Operations Hub throughout while the blueprint commission refers to a Digital Operations Hub.
Site mandate: §4.3.1 states the Site level is mandatory while §2.1 marks the same requirement as an open drafting recommendation.
Job location cardinality: §4.5.1 states one Area per Job as a hard constraint with paired Jobs for multi-Area work; §2.1 supersedes it with one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth.
conflicting_values: one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth (§2.1)

contradictions.description: Record-finish window bounds: §4.6.8 states floor 24 hours and ceiling 7 days while §2.4 carries the same bounds as an open drafting value.
Capture types: §7.8.3 and §5.5.3 each name seven capture types and the sets differ.
conflicting_values: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, e-signature, free text (§7.8.3)
measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or QR scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, dropdown selection (§5.5.3)

contradictions.description: Governance: §5.11.1 says no workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each of three stages, while §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publish a patch with no second approval.
conflicting_values: three-stage sign-off required for all workflow content
Lane-B approval auto-publishes a patch with no second approval and no ceremony

contradictions.description: Action-agent gating: §3.7/§6.6.1 say the runtime gate exists only for proposals beyond pre-authorised policy; §8.3.2 says every action agent routes through a human gate before any effect and §8.3.3 labels the Prevention Agent 'action, gated'.
Roles: §6.13.3 flags an unacknowledged brief on the Plant Manager view while §3.5 fixes five roles, states there is no Quality Director, and makes Plant Manager a persona rather than a role.
conflicting_values: five fixed roles with Plant Manager as a persona (§3.5)

contradictions.description: Package signing: the assignment brief calls the work package 'signed' while the Statement of Work states neither signing nor a validation failure path.
conflicting_values: not specified in the Statement of Work

contradictions.description: Package field assignment: the authoritative field-by-field package-borne versus server-only assignment is said to be carried in the Part VII package contract, and Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: carried in Part VII package contract
Part VII does not enumerate it

contradictions.description: Sync ordering: safety argues commands first so a suspension, wipe or hold lands before more work; data integrity argues captures first so unsynced evidence is never at risk; §7.10.3 explicitly defers payload and ordering semantics.

Library pointer versus pinned package: a library edit propagates to every referencing screen immediately (§5.7) while a run's package is pinned at assignment and never re-based (§5.14, Part II); the interaction for an in-flight run is not stated.

Authority shorthand: source matrices use 'Supervisor+' and 'QM+' without defining an ordering across five additive, non-hierarchical roles, while stating multi-role is additive and audit records identity rather than 'acting as role'.
Containment launcher: whether the device or the agent launches the containment checklist at classification.
conflicting_values: device launches locally from the pinned package (adopted)

contradictions.description: Instruction-level packaging: whether the package carries all three work-instruction difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's level is explicitly open, with the package definition currently carrying all levels.
Gate item display-latency target: the Statement of Work states no display-latency target; §6.2.2 commits only to 'seconds from server receipt' for the pushed class and any numeric target is TBD.
conflicting_values: no numeric target — TBD, Client Decision Required

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A packaged banding that does not cover the observed departure — a gap between bands
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The authoring rule requiring at least one severity mapping per measurement screen, making a gap a publication defect
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A gap occurring at runtime — fail safe: classify to the highest band the mapping defines rather than to none, open the deviation, and flag it band-gap-affected (Recommendation — R&D, not specified in the Statement of Work)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A deviation that is open and conservatively classified rather than a departure that passes unnoticed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected banding published through the Studio chain; reconciliation is the Quality Manager's reclassification with a recorded reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A referenced containment checklist missing from the package
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Package validation at staging, which should have refused the package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Checklist cannot be rendered at runtime — present the deviation record and escalation queue entry without a checklist and mark containment not-launched; the worker follows the plant's own paper containment practice and records it in free text
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A deviation with an explicit missing-containment flag, never a deviation that appears fully contained when it was not
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected package; reconciliation is the Quality Manager's review of the flagged deviation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Escalation delivery failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The escalation is never the containment — containment already happened locally and the deviation record already exists
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Even if the escalation is never delivered at all, the record surfaces at review
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A deviation record that surfaces at review regardless of escalation delivery
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery at reconnection

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The hold failing to persist locally — a storage write error at the instant of classification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry of the transaction (the capture, the classification and the hold commit together)
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Retry fails — the device refuses to accept the capture and instructs the worker to stop work on this lot and call their supervisor
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An unaccepted capture and a stopped operation — deliberately worse for throughput and better for safety
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A device with working storage; reconciliation is the physical containment record and the supervisor's account

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Sibling devices working the same lot do not know about the freeze
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The containment checklist's physical segregation step, which protects the lot on the floor faster than any command channel
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The supervisor's own action once the escalation lands
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The breach point is protected immediately and locally and the rest of the floor converges at sync speed, with every surface saying so plainly
failures_fallbacks.recovery: SB-011 and SB-013; reconciliation is the hold panel showing each device's confirmation timestamp and metered propagation lag

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No Quality Manager on shift when a hold needs disposition
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalations resolve to people on shift; where nobody holding the target role is on shift, delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No Quality Manager responds at all — escalation to the Tenant Admin to secure a Quality Manager, never a widening of authority; no supervisor exception exists by work type, risk class, or tag
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The lot staying frozen indefinitely — a frozen lot costs throughput and an improperly released lot costs a recall
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Quality Manager deciding; reconciliation is the escalation record showing every delivery and fallback marking

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A reviewer disputing a capture's validity
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The append-only annotation, which records the challenge without altering the original
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: There is no path that edits or deletes evidence, on any surface, for any role — that absence is the control
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A record carrying both the original and the challenge
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not applicable

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An anomaly closed without evidence of resolution
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: An anomaly cannot be closed without a closure note
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An anomaly that stays open and ages visibly
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Closure with a note

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command queuing failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Command marked available for delivery per device

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A command a device downloads and cannot validate — a scope mismatch, or a command referring to a hold the device does not hold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Explicit rejection: the device rejects the command, the rejection is acknowledged to the server, and the command moves to rejected rather than being silently discarded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The server re-issues a corrected command after a human reviews the rejection
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device continuing to enforce the hold it holds — the platform fails toward containment
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A valid command applying; reconciliation is the command history showing the rejection and its reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device that never returns
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The honest display: the device is listed as not reached with its last-seen time
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The fleet-side action — the device may be de-authorised from the Super Admin platform console, which faces the same reachability problem (DEC-WIPE-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A lot that remains frozen on the unreached device indefinitely, and a hold that never reaches in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The device returning; reconciliation is the propagation record and lag telemetry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A surface that presents stale data as current
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Every tile and drill view carries a compact sync-state element listing the devices behind the number and when each was last seen
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Freshness computation itself fails — display the marker as unknown with an explicit 'freshness cannot be computed' statement; then degrade affected tiles to a neutral state carrying no status claim
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A board that says what it does not know
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Heartbeat data returning; reconciliation compares the board's last-known picture against the run records with any materially changed aggregate recomputed as an audited event

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device whose clock is wrong enough to corrupt ordering
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Order by server receipt, flag the write, and keep it out of automatic resolution and out of Resolve All
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The reviewing Quality Manager cannot determine which version is correct — neither version is destroyed and the reviewer records an append-only annotation stating the ambiguity, leaving the automatic result standing with a note
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A record carrying both versions, the automatic outcome, and a human's written account of why the ambiguity could not be resolved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A device clock corrected as a fleet action from the Super Admin platform console; reconciliation is a periodic review of skew rates per device

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Ordinary conflicting writes on shared parts of a run
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Automatic resolution — the most recent write wins by device timestamp, both versions preserved, the conflict event audited; the panel never blocks work
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A reviewer judges the automatic resolution wrong — flags it, opening the record's append-only correction path rather than altering the sync result
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Both versions retained with the automatic outcome recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Quality Manager review

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Two conflicting values straddling a specification limit
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The deviation mechanism opens a deviation deterministically
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The evaluation cannot run because the screen's limits are unavailable for the pinned version — raise the conflict to the Quality Manager as an explicit unevaluated quality question rather than closing it as bookkeeping
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An unresolved conflict flagged for quality attention, never a silently closed one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Limits becoming available or a Quality Manager decision

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A capture that fails validation against the run or its pinned package
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Quarantine rather than acceptance or discard; it appears for a human decision
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A quarantined capture that is visible and unresolved, never a silently dropped measurement
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A human decision on the quarantined capture

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Severity bridge failure creating the Critical anomaly
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Not separately elaborated in this chunk

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An agent output that nobody decides
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The acknowledge, timeout and fallback discipline: the item re-routes to the next person per the Studio-authored policy
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The re-route also goes unanswered — the item continues to wait and age visibly; it never executes on its own and never silently expires; the nobody-on-shift default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery (DEC-NOSHIFT-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An item that waits, ages visibly, and never executes; the pre-authorised containment that did happen stands
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A decision at any later point; reconciliation is the item's lifecycle record and its appearance in the shift-handoff brief

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An adjustment that exceeds the authored bounds
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refusal at the bound with the reason stated and a pointer to the authoring path
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Decline-with-reason plus an authoring change request into the Studio, which travels the full three-stage approval chain
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A declined item and an unchanged policy
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Studio authoring change widening what an agent may propose

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Lane A learning-signal recording (case relevance, scope adjustment, annotations)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Signals are logged and reversible and change nothing a person configured

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A Lane-B proposal nobody decides
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The 30-day stale flag copied to the Quality Manager's digest; there is deliberately no expiry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: It continues to age and remains listed, and the configured value simply does not change
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A platform operating on its human-configured values with a visible list of suggestions nobody has acted on
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A decision at any time; reconciliation is the proposal lifecycle record

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An auto-published patch that fails a pre-publication check — an incomplete locale, or a packaging error
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refusal to publish, with the proposal returned to approved-but-unpublished and the condition raised to the Quality Manager and the Studio authors
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual publication through the normal three-stage chain
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The previous version remaining in force with an explicit approved-but-unpublished item outstanding
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A successful publication; reconciliation is the audit chain showing proposal, approval, failed publication and eventual publication

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Version-change command distribution at the next run boundary
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-flight runs finish on the version they started on

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The agent not producing a handoff brief — a platform degradation, or an emergency pause of agent activity
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The honest flag on the agent activity panel plus the underlying data remaining fully available from the board, the alert feed, the deviation workspace and the run records
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A second consecutive failure or any failure outlasting a shift escalates through the standard escalation mechanism; a manual handover is recorded as a note on the shift's record
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A shift that starts with a human-assembled handover and an honest record that the agent did not produce one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The agent returning; reconciliation is the agent activity log showing the gap

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Handoff brief notification failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Both channels used per the configured routing

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Nobody acknowledging the handoff brief
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The visible flag after the 30-minute grace period; there is deliberately no blocking fallback
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The flag has no resolvable target under the five-role model — recommendation is the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery (DEC-HANDOFF-001, not resolved)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An unacknowledged brief that is visibly unacknowledged and a shift that runs anyway
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An acknowledgement at any point

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A clearance that is granted and does not reach the device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command channel's delivery discipline: the clearance is queued and applies at the device's next sync, and until then the block stands
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device does not return within the shift — reassignment of the parked run to a qualified worker through the assignment service
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A parked run and an unqualified worker doing other work — never an unqualified worker proceeding because a notification said a clearance had been granted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The clearance applying at sync; reconciliation is the clearance record showing grant, delivery, application and lapse times

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A qualification-warning digest delivery failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The in-app channel, which is unmutable
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Both channels fail — the block applies on the day regardless
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Unchanged: the failure is that people were surprised rather than that anyone was unsafe
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Channel restoration

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A supervisor not acknowledging the expiry event
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The configured window, default 2 minutes, after which it escalates to the Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Neither responds — the block simply stands and the worker is not assigned; enforcement is the block and not the notification
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An unqualified worker not working on gated steps and a standing signal in the Client Command Center that persists until resolved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A clearance or a recertification; reconciliation is the qualification record and the clearance corpus

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A worker blocked with no other assigned work, which turns parking into idling
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The parked-run model itself, which assumes other assigned runs exist
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where none do — supervisor reassignment through the assignment service, available while the supervisor is online even though the worker's device is not
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A parked run and an idle worker rather than an unqualified worker proceeding — the platform accepts a productivity cost to keep the gate absolute
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Authorisation or reassignment; reconciliation is the run record showing the parked interval and the resumption

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A supervisor believing they can authorise a never-held qualification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The disabled control with its reason, which teaches the rule at the moment it binds
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A supervisor attempting it through a service path — the refusal is recorded as an audit event, because an attempted authority escalation is worth recording
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An unauthorised item waiting for the correct role
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Quality Manager authorisation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Electronic signature capture on screen 11 offline
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Signature committed locally and queued; a forced sync is required only before a designated high-risk sign-off (the supervisor sign-off screen type)
